title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.86): a 'disjoncteur' (E,|∘|_E) is a set with a symmetric 'disjointness' relation. It is extended to subsets by A|∘|B iff a|∘|b for all a∈A, b∈B. supp°_E(A) is the 'support' of A, in effect the bi-orthogonal closure A^{⊥⊥}. Σ_E is the complete lattice of supports. This is what is now called an orthogonality space (Dacey) with its lattice of closed subspaces, i.e. the Galois connection of a symmetric relation.

Two correspondences are given: α: E→P(E') with additive extension ᾱ: P(E)→P(E'), and β: E'→P(E) with extension β̄. Prop. 3 (p.86) states three equivalent conditions.
(i) x|∘|β(x') ⟺ α(x)|∘|x' for all points x, x'.
(ii) The same equivalence for all subsets A, A'.
(iii) The induced maps α_* = supp°∘ᾱ and β_* = supp°∘β̄ between Σ_E and Σ_{E'} satisfy 𝔄|∘|β_*(𝔄') ⟺ α_*(𝔄)|∘|𝔄'. In addition α_*(supp A) = supp(ᾱ(A)), and likewise for β.
When these hold, α and β are called 'transposed' to each other. In modern terms they are adjoint maps between orthogonality spaces, and (α_*, β_*) is an adjoint pair of maps between the closure lattices.

This page, crossed-out part:
- α', β' are defined as the pointwise supports of α(x), β(x').
- An abandoned uniqueness statement: any two transposes β1, β2 of α have the same pointwise supports (β1' = β2') and the same β_* (β1* = β2*). Symmetrically for transposes of β.

This page, the proof:
- (ii)⇒(i): take singletons.
- (i)⇒(ii): disjointness of sets is pointwise, and ᾱ, β̄ are unions.
- Key remark: each side of (ii) is unchanged if either term of the relation |∘| is replaced by its support, since A|∘|B ⟺ supp A|∘|B.
- Hence for A∈Σ_E, A'∈Σ_{E'} the equivalence in (ii) is literally the equivalence in (iii). So (i)⇒(iii), apart from the extra support relations, deferred to 'see below'.
- He then starts (iii)⇒(ii) by rewriting (ii) in support form. This is completed on p.88 via the identities supp(β̄(A')) = supp(β̄(supp A')), proved by an orthogonality argument.

Purpose: build a category of 'disjoncteurs' whose morphisms are transposed pairs of correspondences, inducing adjoint (Galois-type) maps on lattices of supports.
errors: Writes 'A∈Σ_E, A'∈Σ_E'; the second should be Σ_{E'}.
(i)⇒(ii) silently uses that ᾱ and β̄ are the union-extensions of α and β (ᾱ(A)=∪α(x)); this is stated on p.86 only implicitly.
The (i)⇒(iii) step as written covers only the equivalence in (iii). The supplementary relations α_*(supp A)=supp(ᾱ(A)) are deferred ('voir plus bas') and proved on p.88.
The crossed-out uniqueness claim is correct: x⊥β1(x') ⟺ x⊥β2(x') for all x gives β1(x')^⊥ = β2(x')^⊥, hence equal supports. It was abandoned, not wrong.

ideas.what: Set with a symmetric disjointness relation; closure (support) A↦A^{⊥⊥}; lattice Σ_E of closed sets
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality space (Dacey space) and its ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets; polarity/Galois connection of a relation

ideas.what: Transposed correspondences α, β with x⊥β(x') ⟺ α(x)⊥x', and the equivalent lattice-level adjunction
ideas.modern_name: adjointable maps between orthogonality spaces / dagger-category morphisms

ideas.what: Disjointness is invariant under replacing either set by its support, so point-level, set-level and closed-set-level adjointness coincide

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck independently sets up orthogonality spaces ('disjoncteurs') with adjoint ('transposed') correspondences as morphisms. This anticipates the dagger-categorical treatment of orthogonality spaces developed decades later; his precise motivation in the 'Ateliers' chapter is unclear from this page.
missed.quote: on dit alors que α et β sont transposées l'une de l'autre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: Grothendieck working with the same structures as quantum-logic and dagger-category work (Jacobs, Heunen, Paseka–Vetterlein). Mathematically the content on this page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but elementary Galois-connection lemma for symmetric relations. Interest is only that Grothendieck builds the orthogonality-space/adjoint-map framework himself in 1986; the content itself is standard.
